item.question_text: A general insurer builds no models itself. Its claims platform, bought from a vendor, ships with an embedded risk-scoring feature, and its HR suite offers an optional CV-ranking add-on that two teams have switched on. The scoping team is working through context issues before fixing the AIMS boundary. Which approach fits the requirement on understanding context?

options.text: Cover the systems the insurer develops or provides in the context work, and handle the bought-in features through supplier contract review alone.
Postpone deciding the insurer's roles relative to these systems until an impact assessment for each feature has been commissioned.
Take account of what the vendor's scoring and ranking features are meant to achieve where the insurer runs them, alongside anything it builds.
Leave climate change to the interested-party analysis rather than to the determination of context issues.

item.explanation: Clause 4.1 extends context determination to purposes of AI systems the organization merely uses, not just those it builds: the organization 'shall consider the intended purpose of the AI systems that are developed, provided or used by the organization'. Vendor features in use are therefore in view when context is determined.
item.key_support: The organization shall consider the intended purpose of the AI systems that are developed, provided or used by the organization.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The supplier process is an additional control and does not displace considering the purpose of AI systems the organization uses when determining context.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine its roles with respect to these AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Role determination belongs to the context work itself rather than waiting on a later impact assessment.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Relevance of climate change is settled as part of determining external and internal issues, not handed off to the interested-party analysis.

item.question_text: During scoping, a bank lists a financial regulator, a works council, enterprise customers and internal audit, each with stated expectations about its AI use. Several of those expectations will be handled by legal and procurement rather than by the management system. What does the requirement on needs and expectations of interested parties call for here?

options.text: List only the expectations the team has already agreed the management system will take on.
Capture the relevant requirements of each of these parties, then settle which of them the management system will address.
Forward every expectation to risk assessment, which then rules on which parties are relevant.
Confine the analysis to the regulator and the enterprise customers, treating internal functions as covered by policy.

item.explanation: Clause 4.2 requires the organization to determine relevant interested parties, their relevant requirements, and 'which of these requirements will be addressed through the AI management system' — so requirements are captured first and the addressing decision is made afterwards.
item.key_support: The organization shall determine: — the interested parties that are relevant to the AI management system; — the relevant requirements of these interested parties; — which of these requirements will be addressed through the AI management system.

distractor_support.support: the relevant requirements of these interested parties
distractor_support.why_wrong: Relevant requirements of relevant parties are determined regardless of whether the management system will be the vehicle for addressing them.

distractor_support.support: the interested parties that are relevant to the AI management system
distractor_support.why_wrong: Identifying which parties are relevant is part of this determination, not an output of risk assessment.

distractor_support.support: the interested parties that are relevant to the AI management system
distractor_support.why_wrong: Relevance is not limited to external parties; internal bodies such as audit or a works council can be relevant interested parties.

item.question_text: A retailer's AI estate consists of a hosted document-classification service and an analytics product whose vendor added a forecasting model in the latest release. Neither was built in-house. Which action meets the supplier-related control?

options.text: Run a process that checks vendor-provided services and products against the retailer's own approach to responsible AI development and use.
Require each vendor to hold certification against this document before its service may remain in use.
Bring the vendors' own operations inside the retailer's management system boundary and audit them as internal processes.
Keep the hosted service outside the retailer's own arrangements and rely on the vendor's published governance statements.

item.explanation: Control A.10.3 asks for a process ensuring that use of supplier-provided services, products or materials 'aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems' — alignment with the organization's own approach, not vendor certification or absorption of the vendor's operations.
item.key_support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.

distractor_support.support: aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems
distractor_support.why_wrong: The control asks for alignment with the organization's approach, not for supplier certification to the document.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: What is addressed is the organization's own usage of supplier offerings, not the supplier's internal operations as part of its system.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Relying on vendor statements leaves the organization without the process the control calls for over its own usage.

item.question_text: A software company sells an AI platform to other businesses, deploys a third-party language model in its own support desk, and supplies training data to a partner. It is working out its roles relative to these systems during scoping. What can follow from that role determination?

options.text: The roles fix the wording that the documented scope statement has to take.
Roles can narrow the interested parties needing consideration to those holding a comparable role.
Roles are settled by the certification body once it has reviewed the inventory of AI systems.
Which requirements and controls apply, and how far they apply, can turn on the roles the company holds.

item.explanation: Clause 4.1 states that the organization's roles 'can determine the applicability and extent of applicability of the requirements and controls in this document', so applicability and its extent may follow from the roles held.
item.key_support: The organization’s roles can determine the applicability and extent of applicability of the requirements and controls in this document.

distractor_support.support: The scope shall be available as documented information.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The scope must be documented, but no wording is prescribed by the roles determined.

distractor_support.support: External and internal issues to be addressed under this clause can vary according to the organization’s roles and jurisdiction and their impact on its ability to achieve the intended outcome(s) of its AI management system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Roles can make context issues vary, but they do not restrict which interested parties are relevant.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine its roles with respect to these AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Determining roles is the organization's own task, not something assigned by a certification body.

item.question_text: A logistics firm has published a scope statement and an AI policy and has named owners for its intake, evaluation and deployment processes. A reviewer finds nothing describing how those three processes feed one another. Which expectation about the management system applies?

options.text: Interactions between processes are described only where a process crosses a business unit boundary.
The system, the processes it needs and the way those processes interact are established, maintained and documented.
A documented scope statement together with an AI policy is what the requirement for the system asks for.
Process interactions surface through performance evaluation rather than in the documentation of the system.

item.explanation: Clause 4.4 requires the organization to 'establish, implement, maintain, continually improve and document an AI management system, including the processes needed and their interactions', so the interactions are part of what is established and documented.
item.key_support: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain, continually improve and document an AI management system, including the processes needed and their interactions, in accordance with the requirements of this document.

distractor_support.support: including the processes needed and their interactions
distractor_support.why_wrong: No boundary-crossing condition is placed on the interactions that form part of the system.

distractor_support.support: The scope shall be available as documented information.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A documented scope is a separate obligation and does not by itself constitute the established and documented management system.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain, continually improve and document an AI management system, including the processes needed and their interactions, in accordance with the requirements of this document.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Interactions belong to what is established and documented for the system, rather than being left to later evaluation activity.

item.question_text: At a scoping workshop, an investor group and a major customer have each raised expectations about the energy consumption of the firm's model training. A participant asks whether such expectations have any place in the interested-party work for the management system. Which response is sound?

options.text: Expectations of this kind sit outside the management system and belong in sustainability reporting.
Once a party has raised them, climate-related expectations have to be addressed through the management system.
Requirements bearing on climate change can come from relevant interested parties and be captured in this work.
Climate-related expectations are handled as internal context issues rather than as interested-party requirements.

item.explanation: The note to clause 4.2 records that 'Relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change', so such expectations can properly be captured when interested-party requirements are determined.
item.key_support: Relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change.

distractor_support.support: Relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Such requirements are expressly contemplated within the interested-party determination for the management system.

distractor_support.support: which of these requirements will be addressed through the AI management system
distractor_support.why_wrong: The organization decides which determined requirements the management system will address; being raised does not settle that.

distractor_support.support: Relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The note places climate-related requirements with interested parties, so they are not confined to internal context issues.

item.question_text: An insurer runs a claims triage model that is hosted by a vendor, trained on data labelled by an external annotation firm, and operated by the insurer's own claims team. Applying the control on allocating responsibilities, what does this arrangement call for?

options.text: Life cycle responsibilities are apportioned across the insurer, its partners, suppliers, customers and any other third parties involved.
Life cycle responsibilities stay with the insurer, and the two external firms are engaged purely through contractual service terms.
Life cycle responsibilities rest mainly with the vendor that built and hosts the model rather than with the insurer that operates it.
Responsibilities are settled internally to suit the insurer's needs, and external parties are covered by the channel for raising concerns.

item.explanation: The allocating-responsibilities control (A.10.2) requires responsibilities across the AI system life cycle to be allocated between the organization and its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties: "The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties." Keeping them internal, pushing them all onto one supplier, or substituting a concerns channel does not meet that.
item.key_support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The control expects responsibilities to be allocated to the external parties as well, not retained wholly in-house.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Allocation is a sharing out among all the named parties, not a transfer of the life cycle to the hosting vendor.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The concerns-reporting process is a separate control and does not allocate life cycle responsibilities to partners and suppliers.

item.question_text: A start-up asks whether the AI management system controls hand it a fixed roster of AI job titles it has to create. What is the correct understanding of the control on AI roles and responsibilities?

options.text: AI roles and responsibilities are defined and allocated to match what the organization actually needs.
Named owners are mandated for each area listed in the implementation guidance, such as safety, privacy and data quality.
AI roles may be left undefined where existing management system roles already provide general accountability.
AI roles are settled by top management privately and need not be made known beyond the people appointed.

item.explanation: A.3.2 states that "Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization." The areas named in the implementation guidance (B.3.2) are examples that can require defined roles, and that guidance is expressed as should/can rather than as a mandated list; leaving roles undefined, or not communicating assignments, both fall short.
item.key_support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.

distractor_support.support: The organization can prioritize how the roles and responsibilities are assigned.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The listed areas are examples in guidance that can require roles, not a mandated set of named owners.

distractor_support.support: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Defining and allocating AI roles is required, so relying on undefined general accountability does not satisfy the control.

distractor_support.support: Top management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for relevant roles are assigned and communicated within the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Assignments for relevant roles have to be communicated within the organization, not kept to the appointees.

item.question_text: A holding group has drawn its AI management system scope around one analytics subsidiary only. When responsibilities and authorities for relevant AI roles are assigned, who is meant by "top management" in this case?

options.text: Those who direct and control the analytics subsidiary at its highest level.
The group board that directs the whole organization, whatever scope has been declared.
The person given the authority for system conformance and for reporting on performance.
Any subsidiary manager who has been delegated authority and resources for the AI work.

item.explanation: The definition of top management (3.3) notes that where the management system scope covers only part of an organization, top management means "those who direct and control that part of the organization". The group board is therefore not the referent here; the assignee of conformance and reporting authority and any delegate are recipients of authority, not top management itself.
item.key_support: Note 2 to entry: If the scope of the management system (3.4) covers only part of an organization, then top management refers to those who direct and control that part of the organization.

distractor_support.support: Note 2 to entry: If the scope of the management system (3.4) covers only part of an organization, then top management refers to those who direct and control that part of the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: When the scope covers part of the organization, the referent shifts to the direction of that part rather than the whole group.

distractor_support.support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.
distractor_support.why_wrong: That person receives the assigned authority from top management and is not top management.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: Top management has the power to delegate authority and provide resources within the organization.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Holding delegated authority does not make a manager the person or group directing and controlling the organization at the highest level.

item.question_text: A model development house is reviewing the control on reporting of concerns. Which statement describes what that control obliges the organization to have?

options.text: A process for raising concerns about the organization's role regarding an AI system throughout its life cycle.
A process for reporting on the performance of the AI management system to the top management group.
A channel offering confidentiality or anonymity that is staffed by qualified persons with investigation powers.
A process for apportioning life cycle responsibilities between the organization, its suppliers and other third parties.

item.explanation: A.3.3 requires the organization to "define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle." Performance reporting to top management and the allocation of responsibilities are different provisions, and the confidentiality and staffing features sit in the implementation guidance (B.3.3), which is phrased as should.
item.key_support: The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.

distractor_support.support: reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management
distractor_support.why_wrong: That is the assigned authority for performance reporting, a different provision from the concerns-reporting process.

distractor_support.support: The reporting mechanism should fulfil the following functions:
distractor_support.why_wrong: Those features appear in implementation guidance expressed as should, so the control itself does not oblige them.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Allocating responsibilities is a separate control and is not what the reporting-of-concerns control addresses.

item.question_text: A hospital outsources training-data labelling to one vendor and post-deployment monitoring to another. Each vendor assumes the other watches for performance drift, and no one does. How should this be read against the requirement on allocating responsibilities?

options.text: It is a responsibility within the life cycle that has not been allocated between the hospital and its two vendors.
It is tolerable while the hospital keeps overall accountability for the deployed system and its clinical use.
It is a resourcing matter belonging to asset and resource management rather than an allocation question.
It is resolved once the hospital opens a channel for staff to raise concerns about the deployed system.

item.explanation: A.10.2 requires that "responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties" — drift monitoring is such a responsibility, and mutual assumption means it is unallocated. Retained overall accountability does not allocate it, and neither resource management nor a concerns channel closes the gap.
item.key_support: responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties

distractor_support.support: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
distractor_support.why_wrong: General accountability at the hospital does not discharge the requirement to allocate the specific life cycle responsibility among the parties.

distractor_support.support: — asset and resource management;
distractor_support.why_wrong: Asset and resource management is a different area that can require defined roles; the unowned monitoring duty is an allocation gap.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A concerns-reporting process lets issues be raised but does not assign the monitoring responsibility to anyone.
